title: Fecal calprotectin
what: This is a stool test. It shows whether there is inflammation in your bowel.
why: For long-term diarrhea, belly pain, or blood in the stool; to tell bowel inflammation from irritable bowel; and to track treatment.
duration: collecting at home takes a few minutes; results usually come in 1 to 5 days
tell_doctor: If you take painkillers or anti-inflammatory pills. They can raise the result
If you recently had a stomach bug
If you have your period now or bleeding from hemorrhoids

prepare.title: Container
prepare.text: Get a sterile container from the lab or a pharmacy.

prepare.title: Collecting
prepare.text: Collect stool from a natural bowel movement, without enemas or laxatives. Keep urine and water out of the container.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Tell your doctor what you take. They will decide the best time for the test.

prepare.title: Storage
prepare.text: Take it to the lab within the time they gave you.

steps: Pass stool into a clean, dry pot or a bag
Use the scoop in the lid to take a little stool
Put in as much as the lab told you
Close it tightly and label it
feel: Nothing unpleasant, just a little awkward
after: Results usually come in 1 to 5 days
A high calprotectin is a reason for the next step. Your doctor will decide what it is

faq.q: If calprotectin is high, is it a serious disease?
faq.a: Not necessarily. It goes up with any bowel inflammation, including from an infection. Your doctor will find the cause.

faq.q: Why do this test if I can have a colonoscopy?
faq.a: It helps show whether you need a colonoscopy at all. Sometimes you can do without one.

reminders.text: Calprotectin stool test tomorrow. Get the container and a clean pot or bag ready.
